subject: 'Achhe Din' and AI's failed cure
alt: Satish Acharya's cartoon: on a pale beige wall hangs a tall mirror with a thick wooden frame. On the left stands an old man with white hair, a white beard and round glasses, wearing a brown-orange sleeveless jacket over a white kurta; he is looking towards the mirror. Inside the mirror a thin man with long hair and a thick beard sits on the floor, knees bent, head bowed, eyes closed, exhausted; his orange T-shirt says 'ACHHE DIN' and one knee of his blue jeans is torn. On the right a man in a blue shirt, red tie and glasses is speaking, mouth open; his speech bubble says in English: 'SORRY SIR, EVEN AI FAILED TO REVIVE...'. At the bottom right is the cartoonist's signature: SATISH ACHARYA.
chutki: What sits inside the mirror is not a portrait but a patient: 'Achhe Din'. The man in the blue shirt and red tie is giving the old man a report, and it is the same report every time: even AI was tried, and the patient still did not get up. The joke is that every new cure ends up at the same bedside, and the patient does not even turn over.

Acharya's jab is at a promise from 2014 that keeps being revived every season. The technology changes; the patient's condition does not. And when the most advanced engine of all says 'sorry sir' and gives up, the question stops being about the treatment and becomes whether the thing was alive to begin with.
